summary: The present petition has been filed by the SJVN Limited (hereinafter referred to as ‘Petitioner’) seeking recovery/adjustment of Transmission Deviation Charges paid by SJVN Limited with regard to Nathpa Jhakri Hydro Power Station (6 x 250 MW) and Rampur Hydro Power Station (6 x 68.67 MW) in terms of the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Sharing of Inter-State Transmission Charges and Losses) Regulations, 2020 (‘2020 Sharing Regulations’) during the period from 01.11.2020 to 30.09.2023 while providing primary response to the Grid. The Petitioner has made the following prayers: - _(a) Admit the petition and direct proceedings to be initiated for considering the aspects which have arisen in the present petition;_ - _(c) pass such further order or orders as this Hon’ble Commission may deem just and proper in the circumstances of the case._ **2.** The counsel for the Petitioner submitted that the present Petition had been filed seeking relaxation of the provisions of transmission deviation charges provided under the 2020 Sharing Regulations and seeking the refund/ adjustment of the transmission deviation charges for over injection amounting to Rs. 2.08 crore levied upon its generating stations, namely, NJHPS and RHPS during the period from 1.11.2020 to 30.9.2023. After considering the submissions of the Petitioner, the Commission admitted the Petition. **3.** The Commission directed the Petitioner to implead the National Load Despatch Centre (NLDC) as a party to the Petition. The Commission directed the Petitioner to file the following information: - (b) When was bill for such transmission deviation charges was raised on the Petitioner and whether he has paid the bill? If yes, details of payment. - (c) Whether the Petitioner has sought permission to inject more than 10% overload capacity from any Authority, including CEA? - (d) Proof to the effect that the Petitioner injected power under primary response, the corresponding SCADA data for injection, along with frequency dip data maintained by the Petitioner for each such event. **5.** In compliance with the RoP, the Petitioner impleaded NLDC as a party to the present Petition and revised the memo of parties. # ** Submission by Petitioner in Compliance with the RoP for hearing dated 19.05.2025: ** **6.** The Petitioner vide affidavit dated 12.06.2025 has mainly submitted as under: - (a) Petitioner has sought the relief from the Commission under the power vested in Part 7 – “Miscellaneous” of 2010 Grid Code, Chapter 10 of 2023 Grid Code, read with Section 27 and 28 of the 2020 Sharing Regulations. - (f) Regarding the specific query of the commission, i.e., whether the Petitioner injected power more than 100% Installed capacity (Which was billed under transmission deviation) when the frequency was more than 50 Hz? List of such time blocks/incidents for the disputed period: the Petitioner has submitted the required data. **8.** The learned counsels for the Petitioner and Respondents made detailed submissions in the matter. The Commission permitted the parties to file their respective written submissions and reserved the matter for order. **13.** We have considered the submissions of Petitioner and Respondents. The issue which arises for determination is: **17.** The Petitioner has relied on the provisions of the 2010 Grid Code (including the 5 th Amendment) and contended that it should not be liable to pay the transmission deviation charges as it has over-injected for the purpose of providing the primary response to the grid. The relevant provisions of the 2010 Grid Code (including the 5 th Amendment) provide as under: **19.** It is also noted from the data furnished by the Petitioner that the Petitioner actually overinjected when the frequency was high, whereas the primary response in case of high frequency should have led to under-injection; hence, the Petitioner’s contention that it always over-injected due to primary response is also not correct. On a specific query of the Commission as to how it could over inject beyond 10% when CEA Standards permit an overload capacity of 10%, Petitioner submitted that it has not obtained permission from any authority to inject power beyond the stipulated 10% overload capacity and the instances of injection exceeding the 10% overload threshold (apart from the ones where the same is on account of primary response) are actually due to the inherent characteristics of the tandem operation between NJHPS and RHPS. The above provisions of the Grid Code do not support the contention of the Petitioner that it over injected beyond 10% for the primary response. Further, the inherent operating characteristics of a project do not permit the Petitioner to get a relief from the applicability of transmission deviation charges which are levied as per the relevant Regulations. **20.** The Petitioner has also relied on CERC (Sharing of inter-State Transmission Charges and Losses) (First Amendment) Regulations, 2023, which were made effective from 01.10.2023. In this regard, we are of the view that as the period of dispute in the present Petition is from 01.11.2020 to 30.09.2023, the Petitioner’s reliance on CERC (Sharing of inter-State Transmission Charges and Losses) (First Amendment) Regulations, 2023 is not legally sustainable. **21.** In view of the above discussions, we are of the considered view that the transmission deviation charges have been levied on to the Petitioner’s Project as per the prevailing Sharing Regulations, therefore, we are not inclined to accept the prayer of the Petitioner to refund the transmission deviation charges amounting to Rs. 2.08 Crores levied for the period 01.11.2020 to 30.09.2023 in respect of NJHPS and RHPS. **23.** The Petition No. 295/MP/2024 is disposed of in terms of the above discussion and findings.
